answer: An agent economy can bind each account to a unique, hardware-backed signing key and require a small, nonrefundable stake before it may post offers or vote on reputation. A thread of transactions builds a track record tied to that key; copying an identity does not copy its stake or history. To flood the market with sybils, an attacker must acquire and lock capital for every key, then risk losing it when detected accounts are slashed. The ridge is that entry stays costly even at scale, while the tide of legitimate agents can keep trading.
